content.text:
The latest release I could find for the main repo is **v2.11.0**. I couldn't open GitHub directly: the API and page fetch were blocked, and `gh` isn't authenticated. This comes from search-result summaries. The "121 days ago" age on the releases page may be stale, and I didn't confirm v2.11.0 is still the newest.

**v2.11.0 highlights**
- **Keyless access:** the core endpoints (`/scrape`, `/search`, `/interact`, `/parse`) work without an API key from the official MCP, CLI and SDK clients.
- **`redactPII` option:** strips personal and sensitive data from scraped content.
- **`deterministicJson` format:** returns structured JSON without an LLM call on every request. It caches a reusable extractor per site, so repeat scrapes are cheaper and more consistent.
- **Video discovery:** the `video` format now finds videos on any page, not just supported providers.
- **Fixes:** security advisory upgrades (axios, esbuild, ws, openssl and others) across the API and SDKs, plus monitor billing and webhook corrections.

The release before it, v2.10, added a `lockdown: true` option on `/scrape`, which serves results only from Firecrawl's index. It also added a `question` format for `/scrape`.

The separate `firecrawl/cli` repo has its own releases. Its latest listed is v1.23.1, which fixes skill-scoped installs.

If you want the exact date and full notes, the releases page is the place to check.

Sources:
- [Releases · firecrawl/firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/releases)
- [Release Firecrawl v2.11.0](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/releases/tag/v2.11.0)
- [Release Firecrawl v2.10](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/releases/tag/v2.10)
- [Releases · firecrawl/cli](https://github.com/firecrawl/cli/releases)
